title: Powers of ten
mood: from orbit to the one thing
suits: pitches whose story is a change of scale: maps, geo, climate, satellites, data at many resolutions, a fleet down to one vehicle, a codebase down to one line; every slide is a view of one world, and a forward step zooms there.

params.--field / --brand / --brand-2: on the FIRST view's section: the bundled world's sea, shallows, land and coastline derive from them; the sea is the field pushed away from its ink, and every view's --ink-auto is re-picked from it
params.Pack['powers-of-ten'].view(id, cam, { pa: a slide's view: cam = { s px per world unit, x0, y0 } or P.at(x, y, s, cx, cy); paint replaces the world for this picture (P.cells at the bottom of the zoom); frame draws what moves on the one clock
params.Pack['powers-of-ten'].world({ paint(g, c: the deck's own world, painted at any camera (default: the bundled fractal coast, unit 1000 m)
params.Pack['powers-of-ten'].chain('sA>sB', { v: override one move (named levels or views to pass through) or cut it
params.Pack['powers-of-ten'].entry: zoom factor of the establishing dive on a first arrival (default 5; 0 = none)
params..cy-powers-of-ten-vf / .cy-powers-of-ten: viewfinder brackets (lock on after --t s) and the scale caption, both part of the picture

details: the zoom is logarithmic and centred on the point the two views share, so the camera feels like one continuous dive, not a scale tween
a move wider than x12 passes through in-between levels painted from the same world (one per x8), so the coastline gains detail all the way down and nothing pops
the finer picture fades in by scale with feathered (70 px blurred) edges, and the arriving slide's own frame runs live underneath, so its arrival story starts under the move
the bundled coast adds one octave of noise per halving of scale, with each octave rotated, so the shoreline is genuinely fractal at every power of ten
the coastline is drawn bright in a tint of the brand, land carries contours every .08 and a north-west hillshade, and the sea carries fainter depth contours and a pale shelf
the scale caption re-measures itself through the move on a 1-2-5 series (km, then m, then cm) and is part of the picture, not chrome
viewfinder brackets frame exactly what the next slide will show, and lock on with a small scale-in after the move
at the bottom of the zoom the world turns into crisp cells, each the colour sampled at its centre, with a faint per-cell jitter like measured data
the target cell glows once with a ring opening outward on arrival, then breathes very slightly
cloud shadows drift across every view on the one clock, faster the closer you are
the headline zone gets a soft scrim in the world's own sea colour while imagery flies under it, settling into each slide's resting scrim
the sea is the field pushed away from its ink, so headlines read on any brand, light or dark
a first arrival dives in from five times further out, so even a single slide opens with the device
in-between levels and the entry dive are painted while the deck is idle, so the first move does not hitch
print rasterises each canvas to a JPEG at its own rest state, so every slide prints its own view and map-heavy PDFs stay small
